key_insight: A semantic segmentation model can turn whole-slide H&E histopathology images into accurate image-level liver cancer diagnoses by taking the dominant pixel class.
clinical_relevance: This approach may help pathologists triage liver cancer cases and choose immunohistochemical markers more efficiently, potentially lowering cost and turnaround time.
method: Train nnU-Net on pixel-level annotated H&E images from three liver cancer types.
Use stain normalization to reduce variability across specimens and scanners.
Convert segmentation output to an image-level diagnosis using the dominant predicted label.
evidence_signal: In five-fold cross-validation, the model achieved balanced accuracy of 0.975 for HCC, 0.950 for CCA, and 1.000 for CMA on a dataset of 170 images from 89 patients.
watch_item: Performance may be sensitive to annotation noise, staining variation, and limited external validation beyond the collected dataset.
paper_title: Semantic Segmentation-Driven Image-Level Diagnosis of Liver Cancers in Hematoxylin and Eosin Histopathology Images
